title: Prove and repair Wispr Linux shortcut event delivery
description: Generation 173: physical device ACLs are correct and the packaged startup normalization maps absent/Mac-only PTT to 162+91, but the in-app shortcut recorder shows no feedback and Ctrl+Meta has no action. Build a controlled non-user-input evdev-to-pinned-helper-fd3 witness plus packaged Electron receiver witness. Do not inspect runtime Wispr data or alter sessions; use producer lineage 11b2ee0a.
design: Exercise the exact v0.1.2 helper with a controlled virtual keyboard and real fd3 channel, then independently execute the packaged receiver decoder against controlled frames. Change only the terminal producer proven defective; package checks must be Nix checks and a new test must first be observed red.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled Ctrl+Meta press/release produces the exact four KeypressEvent contract frames through pinned helper fd3 and the packaged receiver accepts them. Any proven producer defect is committed and pushed with independent remote eval and check evidence; no live application state is read or changed.
notes: Controlled helper characterization green on producer revision fbb71248567f: remote NixOS VM uses only a private uinput keyboard and an actual fd3 pipe with exact pinned helper v0.1.2. It observed `162 press`, `91 press`, `91 release`, `162 release` KeypressEvent frames with monotonic indexes. No producer helper/protocol defect found. Pre-green failures were harness defects only: missing foreign glibc loader (exit 127) and Python pre-exec fd setup abort; final harness uses nix-ld plus shell fd3 duplication. Receiver runtime intentionally not executed after system topology evidence identified keyd as the live cause.
close_reason: No producer defect: fbb71248567f adds and remotely passes the controlled pinned-helper fd3 NixOS witness. Live keyd virtual keyboard topology remains for the system correction.

title: Restore Linux Ctrl+Meta push-to-talk matching
description: The packaged Linux app receives helper KeypressEvent frames but a stored platform-inapplicable push-to-talk shortcut can never match the Linux Ctrl+Meta physical chord. Determine the proprietary preference schema from the shipped bundle without inspecting runtime preferences. Patch the package so absent or invalid Linux PTT data becomes the exact chord consumed by the current matcher; retain a valid user-selected binding. Add behavioral app and helper fd3 delivery witnesses, expose them as Nix checks, and run them only through configured remote builders. Do not deploy, relaunch, alter session/auth, or change Home/CriomOS pins.
design: Use the existing fix/nix-runtime lineage. Treat non-mac keys as Windows VK values and validate the event stream at the helper fd3 contract boundary. Patch only an evidence-backed, stable bundle site; do not add a compatibility path. Keep runtime data private by making the client-side transformation restricted to the shortcut preference field.
acceptance_criteria: A pre-fix failing behavioral helper witness proves controlled left Ctrl plus left Meta press/release produces fd3 KeypressEvent frames; post-fix it passes through a Nix check. A behavioral app witness proves absent or platform-invalid PTT data becomes the exact Linux Ctrl+Meta matcher chord while an existing valid binding remains unchanged; it too is a Nix check. The producer revision is committed and pushed to the portable fix/nix-runtime ref, with no deployment or runtime preference inspection.
notes: Delivered on fix/nix-runtime 11b2ee0a411f89daedbbff5bd22b640f6a1ddb9a. Remote-only Nix patch and runtime checks passed; full 1.6.7 package build passed. Behavioral startup-contract fixture executes the injected patch: absent or {-1:ptt} maps normalize to 162+91, while a valid custom PTT binding remains. No runtime preference/session/auth data was read or changed; no deploy/relaunch. Coverage gap accepted by repair authority: producer cannot safely add a self-contained helper evdev-to-fd3 VM witness around the pinned binary, so no helper source/repo was changed.

title: Listener can speak the Wispr transcription protocol
description: Listener integration is blocked because Wispr Desktop 1.6.7 exposes no supported local proxy. Prior isolated one-shot requests failed with redacted protocol errors. Reverse engineer the authenticated transcription API from the installed client and existing non-secret evidence without exposing session credentials or private transcript contents.
design: Begin with static bundle and prior-failure analysis. Derive endpoints, transport, request and response schemas, sequencing, and client metadata. Keep credentials behind supported stdin/file-descriptor boundaries. Use synthetic non-private audio for any dynamic witness, and make no billable/backend call until its exact evidentiary purpose is known.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible protocol map identifies endpoint and transport, authentication boundary, request schema, streaming/event semantics, error schema, and transcript result; an isolated witness succeeds on synthetic non-private audio without any secret appearing in arguments, environment, logs, transcript, or repository; findings and implementation are committed and pushed.
notes:
Static map: Wispr 1.6.7 uses TLS gRPC/HTTP2 bidi /flow_api.v1.TranscriptionService/TranscribeStream. Client sends separate queued init/context/audio requests, final commit=TRUE, then half-closes; server may emit heartbeat/state/result. Prior sandbox buffered all frames in one POST and discarded trailers, so ProtocolFailure was non-discriminating. Implementation subflow is building a faithful isolated streaming witness with structural-only diagnostics; no live call yet.
First faithful witness invocation exited 0 before transport at local_stage=bundle-descriptor; HTTP/grpc fields were null and response frame count was zero. No backend call and no transcript-bearing artifact occurred. Current work is correcting the installed-bundle descriptor extraction offline before another attempt.
Offline diagnosis proved the installed app.asar parser succeeds; the first runner had passed the wrong bundle object. A corrected one-shot using the actual app.asar exited 101 before diagnostics, produced only the synthetic audio log, and created no transcript artifact. Current work is removing pre-diagnostics panics and guaranteeing a redacted local-stage artifact for every expected failure before any further live call.
Faithful four-frame bidi gRPC witness reached the service: HTTP 200, content-type application/grpc, grpc-status 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED), zero response frames, no transcript artifact. This proves DNS/TCP/TLS/ALPN/HTTP2, absolute URI, route, RPC path, request submission, and half-close. No inference result. Remaining fork is bearer refresh/session validity versus Baseten static-key/model-route authorization.
Auth discriminator shows the direct default route has bearer_state=fresh, HTTP 200, grpc-status 7, no grpc-message category, zero frames. Faithful EdgeProxy route has bearer_state=fresh, HTTP 200, grpc-status 14 (UNAVAILABLE), one empty frame. Direct model tuple mismatch and stale bearer are not proven causes; next discriminator is a one-shot header-omission matrix, beginning with bearer omitted.
Module-scoped extraction proved the prior runtime selected an unrelated 50-byte literal instead of module-47708 Fo. With the corrected opaque key, the same faithful direct request changed from grpc-status 7 PERMISSION_DENIED to grpc-status 5 NOT_FOUND, fresh bearer, zero frames. This proves the corrected key passes the earlier permission boundary; packaged-default model v31pl413 is not found. Next discriminator selects the client-known ensemble model IDs, beginning with QwenHttp q049l843.
With corrected module-scoped key, qwen-http model, raw PCM packets, and one combined init/context/payload/commit request, the bounded witness returned HTTP 200, grpc-status 3 INVALID_ARGUMENT, one empty frame, fresh bearer, no transcript. This proves live model and authorization; remaining failure is request protobuf semantics. Exact bundle-vs-Rust schema audit is in progress.
